Inclusion met: attacker packs msg.Sender (victim's address) into MsgExecute; checkSender validates against msg.Sender instead of the context sender, allowing the attacker to trigger a fund transfer from the victim's locking account. Object Rebinding BOLA as msg.Sender is the field the system uses to identify the transaction initiator — the attacker overwrites it with the victim's address inside MsgExecute, causing the system to treat the victim's locking account as the transaction source. The authorization failure is the server trusting a client-supplied identity binding field over the authenticated session context. The victim's account is not the target of an action — it is being rebound as the acting identity of the transaction. High confidence from code references, PoC video, and detailed technical explanation.
